name: Religious Fundamentalism
summary: Religious fundamentalism is a family of movements across faiths that insist on the irreducible core of a scriptural tradition and resist secularism, liberalism and modernist reinterpretation. Adherents want scripture or divine law to shape public life, hold firm lines between believers and outsiders, and defend a traditional family and gender order. Economic and constitutional preferences differ widely by tradition.
scope: The cross-religious family as framed by the Fundamentalism Project (reactive, absolutist, comprehensive anti-secular activism), anchored in the Protestant origin (The Fundamentals, the Chicago Statement on inerrancy) with Islamic, Jewish and Hindu variants as context. Where the traditions diverge (clerical rule, apostasy, dress, territory, economics) the profile is neutral or low-confidence; it excludes secular 'fundamentalisms' such as market fundamentalism.

sources.title: Religious fundamentalism (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, cross-religion variation (Christian, Islamic, Jewish, Hindu, Buddhist), politics and secularism.

sources.title: Fundamentalisms Comprehended (Fundamentalism Project, vol. 5), University of Chicago Press
sources.author: Martin E. Marty and R. Scott Appleby (eds.)
sources.usedFor: The project's definition of fundamentalism as reactive, absolutist, comprehensive anti-secular religious activism with family resemblances across faiths.

sources.title: The Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy (1978)
sources.author: International Council on Biblical Inerrancy
sources.usedFor: A founding-type declaration of scripture as supreme, inerrant authority, rejecting science and criticism that override it.

sources.title: The Fundamentals (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The doctrines and targets (higher criticism, evolution, liberal theology, Catholicism, socialism) of the essays that named the movement.

sources.title: Fundamentalism and gender relations: Aires de Familia beyond diversity
sources.author: Monica Tarducci
sources.usedFor: Gender roles and family reorganisation as shared features of Protestant, Islamic and Jewish fundamentalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Fundamentalist movements are defined by religion and moral order, not by health policy; adherents range from charity-first Protestants to welfare-providing Islamist and Haredi networks.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic wage policy is not part of the fundamentalist core; the sources define it by scripture and anti-secularism, and adherents split by tradition and class.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The sources treat economics as peripheral; American Protestant fundamentalists often favor markets while many Islamist and Haredi movements stress communal obligation, so no common line exists.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the conservative religious milieu is generally wary of state economic control, though some movements nationalize or run welfare; not documented as a defining stance.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No defining position in the sources; scriptural duties of almsgiving point one way, conservative anti-tax politics the other.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed by the cross-religious definition; adherents are split between suspicion of secular unions and religiously framed labor groups.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, order-preserving orientation and scriptural protections of property (e.g. commandments against theft), but never a stated fundamentalist tenet.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation is not a fundamentalist question; some adherents want moral regulation of business, others oppose government interference.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents split: many Protestant fundamentalists prefer private charity, while Islamist and Haredi groups run extensive welfare and expect almsgiving; the sources do not settle it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: collective ownership of firms is a secular left program that fundamentalists rarely endorse, though no source discusses it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented position; fundamentalists both fear secular state intrusion and support security measures against perceived enemies.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Fundamentalists stress moral purity and regulation of the family and public behaviour, so recreational drug legalization runs against their moral-order agenda.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists see secular speech codes as targeting their own preaching on sexuality and rival faiths, though some support blasphemy-type limits.

strong-leader.rationale: The Fundamentalism Project notes charismatic leadership inside movements, but political stance on a bypass-the-gridlock leader varies widely by country and tradition.

state-harmful.rationale: Fundamentalism is not anarchist: movements seek to capture or reshape the state to enforce religious order, even while opposing a secular state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: American Protestant fundamentalists typically oppose gun controls, while other traditions have no common line; leaning disagree because of the largest strand.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the order and law-and-order orientation of social conservatism that the sources link to fundamentalism; not a stated doctrine.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Fundamentalist programs reorganize sexual and family life by scripture, and prostitution contradicts its sexual morality in every tradition surveyed.

decide-locally.rationale: No cross-religious stance; some strands favor communal autonomy against a secular centre, others national religious law.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents mix redemptive emphasis with punitive scriptural justice.

traditional-family.rationale: Tarducci describes concern for the domestic sphere and programs to reorganize family life by religious values as a shared feature across Protestant, Islamic and Jewish fundamentalism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to LGBT rights among fundamentalist politics, and family-centered scriptural norms make marriage between a man and a woman non-negotiable.

abortion-legal.rationale: Wikipedia names opposition to abortion as a standard fundamentalist political position, rooted in scriptural views of life.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Fundamentalism Project defines fundamentalism as a comprehensive, anti-secular activism seeking to give religion a central place in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a fundamentalist-defining question; attitudes vary by country and movement, with some stressing individual conversion over structural remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Fundamentalist gender models rest on God-ordained roles for men and women, which contradicts the view of gender as mainly social construction.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Fundamentalists seek to preserve a religiously defined tradition against secular erosion, which usually extends to national cultural heritage, though loyalty is to the faith first.

gradual-change.rationale: Fundamentalism is reactive and activist, aiming to recover a purer order rather than respect existing secular institutions; adherents see gradualism as accommodation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Splits by setting: Protestant and Hindu nationalists often favor restriction, while minority fundamentalists in the diaspora or churches active in migrant ministry differ.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: universal secular institutions are viewed as vehicles of secularism and relativism by the sources' description of anti-secular movements.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no cross-religious economic line exists.

nation-first.rationale: Loyalty is to the religious community, which may be national (Hindutva, religious Zionism) or transnational (Salafism, evangelical missions), so the answer splits.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists tend to distrust secular human-rights framing and Western interventions, but movements differ widely.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: boundaries between in-group and out-group are central to the definition, which is at odds with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: environmental limits on growth are a secular progressive cause; fundamentalists, especially in the US, usually oppose them though some stress stewardship.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the political alignment the sources describe with social conservatism; not stated as doctrine.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Fundamentalists use modern technology instrumentally but see human problems as moral and spiritual, so reject the claim that technology will solve most of them.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No relation to fundamentalist doctrine; stance varies by country.

revolution-justified.rationale: Splits sharply: Iranian revolutionaries and jihadists endorse it, whereas Protestant and many Haredi fundamentalists reject political revolution. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Fundamentalists reject secular expert authority where it contradicts scripture, as the Chicago Statement does on science and criticism, and place authority in scripture and religious leaders.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: central planning is associated with secular socialism, which Christian fundamentalist writings warned against; no direct source on other traditions.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between family-property conservatism and scriptural duties toward the poor.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not a religious question; adherents vary by country.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wage labour is a communist aim, and Christian fundamentalist writing warned against socialism and communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No relation to doctrine, though some Islamist strands oppose interest-based banking.

one-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists want religion, not a party ideology, to lead the state, though in Iran a clerical movement dominates; generally not framed as a single party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Splits: Saudi Salafism accepts a monarchy, Shia and Protestant fundamentalists do not insist on it.

democracy-best.rationale: Fundamentalists generally subordinate popular will to divine law, so they do not hold democracy to be best even when voters choose badly, though many participate in elections.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; no consistent position across traditions.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: councils of workers as the basis of power are a secular socialist model foreign to religious authority.

right-to-secede.rationale: Depends on whether secession serves the faith; no common stance.

natural-rulers.rationale: Some strands hold that scholars or the pious should lead, others do not; the sources do not show a shared view.

political-violence-never.rationale: Many fundamentalists reject pacifism and some endorse violence (anti-Muslim riots, jihadism); but many movements are non-violent, so the typical answer is disagree.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a defining stance; militant strands glorify struggle but many movements do not.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Fundamentalism Project defines fundamentalism as anti-secular religious activism, and Wikipedia describes it as opposing secularist currents, so strict separation is rejected.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Comprehensive anti-secular religious activism seeks to base public law on scripture, as with Islamist sharia programs, Jewish halakhic and Christian theonomist movements.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists want religious courts and state enforcement of moral law, not commercial provision; no source addresses it.

military-superiority.rationale: Not a doctrinal matter; varies by country and movement.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Splits between faith-defined community and ethnoreligious movements such as Hindutva or religious Zionism; religion rather than ethnicity is the usual line.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class conflict as history's driver is a Marxist thesis; fundamentalists see history as governed by God and moral struggle, and Christian fundamentalist writing warned against communism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists emphasise divinely ordered roles and moral desert over enforced equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; some fundamentalist strands with indigenous traditions differ from settler-religious ones.

colonial-reparations.rationale: No documented position; Islamist movements may favor it, Western Protestant ones usually not.

civilizational-union.rationale: Transnational religious unity is central for Salafi and pan-Islamic strands but Protestant fundamentalists and national religious movements do not seek political unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred: scriptural ethics stress duty to God and neighbour over self-interest as the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Fundamentalist movements subordinate individual autonomy to divine commands and communal moral duty, as with sharia-first views of rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; adherents often hold nature as God's creation with stewardship, but this is not a doctrinal fundamentalist line.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from the concern for family and procreation and opposition to abortion and contraception in many fundamentalisms.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fundamentalism is reactive against modernity's values rather than its industry; adherents use modern technology widely.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Fundamentalists oppose technology-driven disruption of traditional social order, though they adopt modern media effectively.

human-enhancement.rationale: Altering human nature through technology conflicts with scriptural views of creation, in line with opposition to secular modernism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: authority is placed in God and scripture and religious leaders, not algorithms.

restore-past-order.rationale: Wikipedia defines fundamentalism by an emphasis on a return to an earlier ideal of purity, and the Fundamentalism Project calls it a reaction against secular erosion of traditional society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Absolutist adherence to irreducible beliefs is the defining mark, so policies are judged by faith, not by pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: Movements range from electoral parties to street action and violence; the sources show a mix.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not documented as a shared principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts the traditional, scripturally ordered community fundamentalists want; no tradition advocates foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist programs assign distinct roles to men and women and to clerics and laity.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Almsgiving is a scriptural duty in many traditions, but distribution by need as the economic principle is not a fundamentalist doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist exploitation theory of profit is rejected by religious fundamentalists, who warned against socialism and communism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A class dictatorship is incompatible with religious authority and was denounced in fundamentalist texts as communism.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred: collective farming is a communist program; fundamentalists have no stake in it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: Marxist theory of imperialism is not adopted; Islamist writers may blame the West but for religious reasons.

taxation-theft.rationale: No doctrinal line; zakat and tithes are scriptural but state taxation views vary.

harm-principle.rationale: Fundamentalists want the state to enforce scriptural morality beyond harm to others, in sexual conduct, blasphemy and family law.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists often place community and divinely given norms above individual rights; sharia-first views of rights are an example.

conscription.rationale: Not a doctrinal question; some exempt religious students (Haredi), others support it.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: state is seen as an instrument of moral order, not a customer-service business.

media-academia-power.rationale: Fundamentalists see secular universities and media as hostile powers undermining faith; the Chicago Statement rejects the authority of higher criticism in academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a religious doctrine; religious universalism generally opposes racial hierarchy, though some strands diverge.

total-state.rationale: The movements seek religious order across all of life but through religious law and community; a state directing culture and economy as such is not their model, though theocracies approach it.

national-rebirth.rationale: Fundamentalist movements share a language of decadence and revival, a return to an earlier faith, but the rebirth they seek is religious more than national.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Splits: religious Zionist and jihadist strands expand, Protestant and Haredi fundamentalism generally does not.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred: no modern fundamentalism advocates bound agricultural labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Fundamentalists hold that truth is fixed by revelation and not by power, but they do claim secular knowledge reflects presuppositions; split.

universal-morality.rationale: They hold universal moral truths grounded in revelation, though they deny that reason alone discovers them; the Chicago Statement makes scripture the supreme norm.

single-common-good.rationale: The comprehensive, absolutist outlook holds one divinely given good for society rather than a balance of interests, though it is derived from revelation rather than reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Religious Zionists strongly agree, Haredi groups historically doubt a secular state, and Christian and Muslim fundamentalists differ.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Depends on the faith and homeland; no common line.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not a doctrinal question, though Haredi attitudes to Hebrew differ.

school-vouchers.rationale: Fundamentalists prefer religious schooling and parental control of education, so public vouchers for any school suit them.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; mixes of moral example and enforced law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Depends on whether the nation is religiously defined; no common line.

force-without-un.rationale: Attitudes to unilateral force abroad split: American Protestant fundamentalists often back it, Islamist movements oppose Western interventions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Chicago Statement makes scripture, not human reason, the supreme norm and denies that scientific hypotheses may override it, and fundamentalism is defined against secular rationalism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not a doctrinal matter; moral-conservative views of dependency vary.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred: the conservative moral order emphasises harmony and cooperation over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Fundamentalists want to retain and recover inherited tradition, so sacrificing cultural institutions for new creation contradicts that aim.

dominated-front.rationale: Islamist strands endorse anti-Western fronts, while American fundamentalists do not; split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Tarducci identifies gender relations and distinct sexual roles as a central feature of fundamentalist rhetoric and practice across Protestant, Islamic and Jewish movements.

ban-interest.rationale: Islamic fundamentalists support it on scriptural grounds, Christian and Hindu ones do not.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a doctrine of the cross-religious family; some historic American fundamentalists defended segregation, but as a religious movement it is not definitional.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state is rejected in fundamentalist writings against communism.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the alignment with American conservatism in the largest strand; not a doctrine.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Depends on the context; minority fundamentalists resist assimilation while majority ones may demand it.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not an established fundamentalist doctrine; some strands share conspiracy views but the sources do not show a common one.

national-mission.rationale: Missionary and evangelising zeal is common, but a national mission to spread a form of government is not a shared fundamentalist tenet.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Fundamentalists regard male headship as divinely ordered rather than as a system of disadvantage, so they reject the claim that society is organised to advantage men over women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists commonly depict secular elites as morally corrupt, but the sources do not document it as a tenet.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Religious teaching on the sanctity of life and procreation makes eugenic restriction objectionable to fundamentalists.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movements want a state that enforces moral order, so minimal government limited to defence and property does not fit.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a general fundamentalist doctrine; many warn against interreligious not interracial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Universal creation in God's image supports equal worth of persons, though fundamentalists deny equal rights between believers and non-believers or between sexes.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Splits sharply between religious Zionists and Islamists; no common line.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Fundamentalist movements want religious personal law applied to their community, so a single civil code regardless of religion is opposed, except where the majority faith wants one (Hindutva).

restrict-conversion.rationale: Many bar conversion away from their faith but champion proselytism of others, so the issue splits by who benefits.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Specific to Hindu fundamentalism; others have no stake.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Anti-secular movements want religion in public life, including state schools through school prayer, which Wikipedia lists as a fundamentalist cause.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine with no counterpart in religious fundamentalism, which has no position on withering of the state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority is held to derive from God and scripture, not from the consent of the governed; many strands nonetheless operate within democracies.

population-transfer.rationale: Some militant strands have supported expulsion, but typical fundamentalists have no such doctrine, and many religions condemn it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Absolute non-aggression is a libertarian principle; fundamentalists accept punitive and defensive force in service of religious law.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred: progress is seen as moral and spiritual, not driven by struggle; Christian fundamentalists also reject evolutionary struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Splits: they resist bans on religious parties but would favor outlawing anti-religious ones.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; fundamentalists differ in constitutional preferences.

vanguard-party.rationale: Charismatic leadership exists, but the Leninist model of a revolutionary party for the working class is not theirs.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from scriptural duties of charity common to all the major traditions, but not a defining stance.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: pronatalist religious views reject population limits as the explanation of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Strong in-group boundaries favor homogeneity of faith, but ethnic diversity as such is not addressed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: No common stance; varies with whether the movement is in power.

party-controls-media.rationale: Movements in power often censor media for religion, but this isn't about a ruling party; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagree because it is a communist-style principle.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists distrust supranational secular institutions, though a religious supranational polity can appeal to some.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Depends on denomination: Protestant fundamentalists mostly congregational, while Catholic and Orthodox traditionalists hold episcopal views.

clerical-rule.rationale: Iranian-style clerical rule is the Shia revolutionary model, but Protestant, Sunni and Hindu fundamentalists generally reject rule by senior clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists reject anti-war defeatism, which is a Marxist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Programs to reshape morality, family life and education by religious values commonly include censorship of material seen as corrupting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Split between American gun-rights fundamentalists and those favoring state monopoly.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: the modern-urban, secular city is identified with moral decline in fundamentalist rhetoric, but not a stated doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Fundamentalists distrust university elites, especially higher critics and liberal theologians who the Chicago Statement and The Fundamentals oppose.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Fundamentalists hold their own religion true and others false, and The Fundamentals attacked Roman Catholicism and other groups as errors.

death-penalty.rationale: Scripturally anchored punishment of grave crimes is widely endorsed, though not all fundamentalists agree; Wikipedia ties them to strict moral law. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education and gender equality teaching clash with the fundamentalist concern over children's education and sexual roles.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Chicago Statement forbids letting scientific hypotheses overturn Scripture on creation, and The Fundamentals promoted creationism and opposed evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Fundamentalist programs seek to restore sexual and family morality through law, so restriction of pornography is typical.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Fundamentalists often seek exemptions from laws burdening their practice, though they may deny the same to other minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The emphasis on purity and conformity to a scriptural norm runs against encouraging nonconformity.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Charity is a religious duty, but international redistribution has no common stance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Religious Zionists and some Hindu and Islamist movements say yes on sacred territory, while most Protestant and Haredi fundamentalists have no such position.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; fundamentalists simply reject Soviet communism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Anti-secular religious activism seeks to protect religious institutions from the state, so curbing clerical power is rejected. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Most monotheistic fundamentalists deny divinity or divine descent to a ruler, since divine authority is vested in scripture, though some regard rulers as divinely appointed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fundamentalist anthropology holds human beings are fallen by nature and morally accountable, not shaped mainly by circumstances.

leader-cult.rationale: Charismatic leadership occurs in movements, but state portraits and statues of a leader as embodiment of the nation conflicts with iconoclastic traditions.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; the traditional family stress may favor maternal custody, but this is unclear.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis about socialist society that religious fundamentalism neither adopts nor addresses.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Sharia fundamentalists affirm it and some Hindu and Jewish ones accept sanction; Protestant fundamentalists reject civil punishment, so adherents split.

women-must-cover.rationale: Strongly supported by Islamic fundamentalists and some Haredi groups, opposed by Protestant and Hindu ones; Tarducci notes the concern but does not make it universal.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fundamentalists see history as ruled by divine providence and moral struggle, and reject the Marxist materialist claim.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Required equal representation of women and men in public bodies contradicts distinct male and female roles central to fundamentalist programs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral and religious motivation is valued but not as replacement for material incentives; split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Militant strands accept it, most others do not.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Fundamentalists want education centered on their own religious tradition and heritage rather than neutral secular curricula.

patriotic-education.rationale: Loyalty is first to the faith; patriotic pride is supported by American and Hindu strands and not by others.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; some seek private religious freedom to refuse services, but the sources are silent on a general principle.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: a legislature cannot override divine law, so parliamentary supremacy is not fundamentalist doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Fundamentalism is defined as activism and involvement in public life, though some separatist strands withdraw.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist authority rests on scripture and its interpreters, not on feudal oaths between lords and followers.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred: a secular-left economic program with no basis in scripture-centred fundamentalism, which tends toward conservative economics.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Religious fundamentalism has no doctrine on fiscal policy; movements range from austerity-minded American conservatives to spending Islamist states.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Adherents split between community-first welfare for coreligionists and universal charity, and the sources do not settle which prevails.

workers-nation.rationale: Movements organise on religious lines rather than class lines, so neither national nor international class organisation is a fundamentalist position.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not a fundamentalist concern; they use whichever system helps religious parties.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Splits by whether the abuses were by or against the movement; no doctrine.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade policy has no link to fundamentalist doctrine.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not addressed; fundamentalists define freedom as obedience to God.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are unrelated to the religious agenda the sources describe.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: No documented position; conservative leanings suggest mild support, religious labour movements exist.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: authority is meant to go to the pious and learned, not to random citizens.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not a religious question; Islamic tradition has debates on price fixing and others do not.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration rules are unrelated to doctrine; minority and majority strands differ.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not a fundamentalist issue.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Movements stress discipline within the community, but binding party members is a political-organisation matter the sources do not cover.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive-legislative balance is not a doctrinal issue.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: No doctrine; religious regimes vary from clerical rule to elected parties.

recall-officials.rationale: Procedural democratic tool not addressed by fundamentalist writing.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Foreign policy attitudes vary: Salafists oppose Western bases, American fundamentalists back allies such as Israel.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: a communal-egalitarian housing mandate lacks scriptural basis and the conservative property outlook opposes it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Depends on the religious stake in the specific nation; no general doctrine.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not part of the fundamentalist definition; faith not descent is the boundary.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is a secondary issue; adherents back language of scripture or their community.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Jubilee debt forgiveness is a scriptural theme, but fundamentalists do not make international debt a defining issue.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economic transformation is a left idea, not part of religious fundamentalism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Procedural question; movements seeking religious constitutions may prefer clerical drafting but some use assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Development-first authoritarianism is not a religious position.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Depends on the state; no doctrine.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Procedural question with no doctrinal answer.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside the sources' account of fundamentalism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Religions teach stewardship and almsgiving yet defend property rights; fundamentalism does not resolve this.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: environmental regulation is part of the secular-progressive agenda to which American fundamentalists are largely opposed.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance attitudes vary by country and are not doctrinal.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Depends on the religious stake in the territory.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Depends on which religious community is seceding.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Depends on whether the region is religiously autonomous; no common stance.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is not a fundamentalist doctrine, though tithing is a flat share in some traditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Fundamentalists hold rulers are bound by divine law; the Chicago Statement puts scripture as supreme norm binding conscience, so rulers are not above law.

land-redistribution.rationale: No cross-religious position; some Islamist movements back it, others defend property.

refugee-return.rationale: Depends on the religious group involved; no common line.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Some religious-nationalist strands claim territory, but this is not general.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not part of the doctrine, though some fear a one-world economic order.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity is sought on religious not ethnolinguistic lines.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist minorities generally seek autonomous religious schools and institutions, as in Haredi enclaves.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minorities differ between staying and emigrating to a religious homeland.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not a doctrinal issue.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are unrelated to doctrine, though moral-hazard arguments appeal to conservatives.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: where fundamentalists are a majority they resent secular courts overriding religiously inspired laws.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Splits by country; Sunni monarchies and Shia clergy have hereditary elements.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Missionary traditions lean yes historically, but fundamentalist movements often resent Western tutelage; split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from alignment with social conservatism in the largest strand, not a doctrine.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary system design is not a doctrinal issue.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist crisis theory is not addressed by fundamentalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Specific to certain states (e.g., Ottoman nostalgia); no general stance.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not doctrine; Islamist writers sometimes criticise the West while embracing trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist-Leninist theory that fundamentalists do not use.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Secular rights charters are viewed with suspicion where they override religious law, but US fundamentalists defend constitutional rights; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Procedural; religious legitimacy matters more than the selection method.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist communities place authority in religious leaders and scripture rather than unanimous consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that divine law binds rulers; many strands justify resisting rulers who violate it, though Protestant ones are cautious.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Humane animal treatment is taught in several traditions, but animal sentience as a moral claim is not a fundamentalist theme.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: scripture grants humans dominion over animals and permits their use with limits on cruelty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from charity duties in the scriptures of the major traditions.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Fundamentalists criticise mass media as corrupting rather than pacifying; the statement's meaning is critical-theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Critical-theory hegemony is not part of the fundamentalist view.

native-born-offices.rationale: Religious tests matter more than birth.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No doctrine; Islamist writers sometimes favour self-reliance.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; fundamentalists criticise secularism not fascism specifically.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Christian fundamentalist writing condemned communism, and fundamentalists generally oppose both secular ideologies.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Specific American historical claim, not doctrine.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the traditionalist wish to preserve inherited heritage extends to monuments in many cases.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: critics of feminist programs among fundamentalists often argue for attention to men and boys too, though the sources do not document it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not documented; fundamentalists generally oppose violence in the home but dispute gendered framing.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Fundamentalists reject Western secular institutions in favour of religiously based forms of government, as in Islamist programs.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Splits: Turkish and Egyptian militaries opposed Islamists, others back them.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists emphasise home as women's sphere of unpaid service rather than recognised labour, but this is not stated.

filial-duty.rationale: Respect for parents is a commandment in the scriptures of the major traditions and a core of the family order fundamentalists defend.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not addressed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Corporate takeover policy has no doctrinal tie; nationalist strands may support blocking, free-market strands oppose it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Fundamentalist family programs resist easy divorce, as the traditional marriage is a scriptural institution.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: land belonging to the community conflicts with the conservative defence of private property.

single-official-language.rationale: Sacred languages are central for some traditions, but a sole official tongue is not a doctrine.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Barring foreigners from owning land follows nationalist rather than religious lines, so adherents split by country.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from opposition to progressive equity policy.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Fundamentalists criticise materialism as part of modernity's moral decay and call for simplicity.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Mixed; some Islamist jihadi supporters and American hawks support, others oppose.

corporate-influence.rationale: Splits between populist anger and pro-business conservatism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Mixed; governments with Islamist ties restrict foreign NGOs, while evangelicals welcome foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Concern for the family and children and opposition to birth limitation make family incentives attractive to fundamentalist programs.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Fundamentalists hold obedience to lawful authority is owed as God-ordained, though divine law outranks human law.

non-intervention.rationale: Absolute non-intervention splits adherents: jihadist and missionary strands intervene abroad, while quietist ones do not.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Some strands hold conspiracies, but the sources do not show it as shared; split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage as a recognised institution is central to fundamentalist family programs.

informal-organisation.rationale: Fundamentalist movements are typically organised around established religious authority.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: opposition to supranational secular norms favours national religious or constitutional law, but Salafis reject nation-states.

religious-nation.rationale: Fundamentalist movements tend to define communal belonging by religion, but strands such as Protestant ones in plural countries do not demand it legally.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: tribute to a foreign power conflicts with religious sovereignty.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist formula; fundamentalists defend private property generally.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Fundamentals warned against communism and fundamentalists regard atheist communism as an enemy.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: faith-based providers inside funded systems fit their wish for religious schools and hospitals.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Chicago Statement and fundamentalist doctrine assert that scripture is God-given truth, directly contradicting the view that religion is a consoling illusion.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: equality of women is not the aim, so the economic-change thesis is not accepted.

socialized-care.rationale: Fundamentalist family programs place childcare and housework within the family, specifically with women.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Some separatist communities exist but communal property is not a doctrine.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Islamist writers have claimed a third way, but Protestant fundamentalists back capitalism; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Religious Zionists and Hindu nationalists affirm sacred claims; others do not, so adherents split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The claim is a conspiracist falsehood; fundamentalism as such does not include it, though some Islamist writers deny it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Opposition to LGBT rights is a standard fundamentalist politics, but criminal sanction varies, strongest in Islamist strands.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Depends on whether movement is in power; no doctrine.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religious activism favoring strict religious order commonly seeks blasphemy laws, though Protestant fundamentalists do not seek civil punishment. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Specific to Islamic fundamentalism, where it is affirmed; other traditions do not have the concept.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Strongly held by jihadist and Islamist revolutionaries, rejected by Protestant, Haredi and quietist Salafi fundamentalists.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical-theory framework that fundamentalists reject.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Wikipedia ties fundamentalist politics to opposition to LGBT rights and gender relations are fixed by scripture.

assisted-dying.rationale: Fundamentalist teaching on the sanctity of life, which also underlies opposition to abortion, rejects assisted dying.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The absolutist, oppositional stance treats politics as a moral contest, not a blend.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Christian fundamentalists often agree, Muslim ones disagree.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Chicago Statement affirms scripture as God's authoritative word binding conscience, and fundamentalism holds that sovereignty rests on divine revelation. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Wikipedia notes fundamentalist protest against headscarf bans, and anti-secular activism rejects limits on religious dress.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pacifism is not fundamentalist; militant strands see force as legitimate and most accept defence.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Islamic strands favor interest-free finance, others do not.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Eco-feminism is rejected by gender-role traditional movements.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Fundamentalists hold fixed written law, scripture, over case-by-case rule, but sources do not address decrees.

racial-franchise.rationale: Not a general tenet; universal religions reject race-based franchise.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Strong in-group boundaries lead many fundamentalist movements to resist marriage across faiths, as in Islamic and Haredi law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Some strands boycott, but this is not a general doctrine.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Chicago Statement denies later revelation corrects earlier and rejects readings that discount the text; Wikipedia says fundamentalists reject modernist reinterpretation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to LGBT rights as a fundamentalist political cause.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Fundamentalism is an anti-secular activism; state-promoted atheism is exactly what it fights. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: religious moral order requires enforcement; abolition conflicts with that.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Private and religious charity is favored by many Protestant fundamentalists and religious networks, though Islamist states fund welfare.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Tarducci identifies male-female roles as central, and fundamentalist traditions typically reserve clerical offices for men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Headship of the husband is a fundamentalist teaching; shared authority is the modern view they reject.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism is not fundamentalist doctrine.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Sex roles ordained by God contradict social constructionism.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Fixed gender categories are basic to the gender roles fundamentalists defend.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring those who die for faith as martyrs is central to militant strands; for the nation specifically, moderate.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Fundamentalism Project (s2) defines fundamentalism as absolutist religious activism that draws a sharp line between the faithful and their enemies, which casts politics as a struggle between good and evil. No cited source states the formula itself.

god-not-male.rationale: Traditional male language for God is retained in fundamentalism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The Chicago Statement makes scripture the supreme norm that judges, not is judged by, outside standards.

family-wage.rationale: A male breadwinner earning enough to support the family fits fundamentalist gender roles.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Fundamentalist doctrine holds human beings have a spiritual nature and soul and expects politics to serve religious ends. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Fundamentalist movements hold that women have distinct God-given roles and virtues in the home.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Whether colonial borders should stand depends on the religious stake; Islamist writers reject Western-drawn borders, but Protestant fundamentalists have no view and the sources record none.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist movements usually claim leadership for believers of their own faith, not for descendants of pre-colonial peoples as such, though indigenous revivalists differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: authority rests with scripture and its recognised interpreters, so binding leaders to voters' mandate runs against the model, though it is not stated.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design has no tie to doctrine; American conservatives lean to private accounts while Islamist and Haredi communities rely on community support.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Fiscal procedure is not touched by the sources; religious regimes range from parliamentary Islamist parties to clerical oversight bodies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: Islamist and Protestant movements generally resent foreign troops dictating a state's political system, though they do not discuss alliance discipline.

residents-only-property.rationale: Communal land restrictions appear in some religious enclaves but are not a general fundamentalist claim.

job-guarantee.rationale: State employer-of-last-resort policy is not discussed; religious charity traditions offer work and aid but fundamentalist parties differ on state economics.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists do not hold democracy to be the best form, and they see moral and religious conflict, not regime type, as the driver of peace and war.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation form is a labour-movement issue with no fundamentalist doctrine.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not addressed in sources; movements as opposition favour it and as rulers often restrict it.

local-production.rationale: Some religious communities favour local self-sufficiency, but it is not a defining stance of the sources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism depends on the regional position of the movement, with no doctrinal rule.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Protestant fundamentalists often praise capitalism while Islamist writers criticise it; the sources show no common view.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism appears in some religious nationalisms (Arabic or Sanskrit revivalism) but is not shared across traditions.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not a religious question; no source gives a fundamentalist position on treaties with indigenous nations.

majority-settlement.rationale: Encouraging majority settlement in minority regions appears in some religious nationalisms (Hindutva, religious Zionism) and not others.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists locate authority in scripture and religious leaders, so broad participatory decision making in workplaces and universities is not their model.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Conservative religious movements oppose sexual harassment but have taken no common stance on contract law for complaints.

social-market-economy.rationale: A social market economy partly echoes Christian democratic thought, but fundamentalists are not tied to it and economic views vary.

rich-first.rationale: Prosperity-first economics has no doctrinal basis here; the prosperity gospel in some Protestant strands accepts it, others do not.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alignment depends on the state; Islamist movements have both sought non-alignment and joined blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Sunni Gulf monarchies are dynastic and Salafi, but Shia, Protestant and Hindu fundamentalism have no such rule.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Debt conditionality is not addressed; Islamist parties have been critical of the IMF while others cooperate.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists tie authority to religious standing rather than wealth, and most operate in mass-franchise systems.

reification.rationale: A Marxist notion unrelated to the scripture-based view; fundamentalists would reject its materialist social theory.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Fundamentalists distrust secular media for its values, not primarily for ownership by the wealthy.

online-participation.rationale: Fundamentalist movements use the internet heavily for preaching, but no source addresses online deliberation or decision making.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency of administrative records is not a fundamentalist issue.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: randomly selected citizens deciding public questions conflicts with the idea that scripture and its interpreters guide the community.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Scripture warns about wealth, but fundamentalism as a political family has no shared view that wealth threatens liberty.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power sharing is used by religious parties in Lebanon and Iraq but opposed by those who want one religious law; no common stance.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are procedural; religious leaders often hold life-long office but elected religious parties accept limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not addressed by sources and has no doctrinal link.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Many fundamentalists expect an eschatological end according to scripture, which makes policy on extinction risk a low priority, but the sources give no stance.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: in-group and out-group boundaries are central to fundamentalism, which points against giving non-citizens a vote.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not a fundamentalist concern.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is a commercial matter outside the sources' description.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Youth organisations with uniforms exist in some movements (Brotherhood scouts, Hindutva shakhas) but not across fundamentalism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons has no doctrinal line.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Salafi and Islamist movements oppose foreign troops in Muslim lands, but American fundamentalists support US bases; the family splits.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition depends on which past killings are at issue and who suffered them, with no shared stance.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Marxist-style claim is not endorsed, yet scriptural opposition to interest overlaps with it in Islamic strands; split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Religious nationalists claim continuity from sacred origins, but Protestant fundamentalists do not emphasise national continuity.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Depends on the religion and diaspora; religious Zionism and Haredi views on Israel differ.

culture-before-state.rationale: Fundamentalists regard religious renewal of society as central, but whether it must precede state power varies between quietist and political strands.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Where the movement is in the majority it sometimes seeks it (Malay or Sinhalese Buddhist), but it is not a shared doctrine.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative borders for peoples are not a fundamentalist issue.

independent-unions.rationale: Independence of unions has no doctrinal link; Islamist movements have both sponsored and opposed independent unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialism is rejected; the statement concerns what makes socialism genuine, and fundamentalists would not accept its premise.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of local utilities is not a religious matter.

second-chamber.rationale: Some Islamist constitutions create councils of religious scholars as a second body, but the statement is not a general fundamentalist position.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: communal ownership of production is a socialist or anarchist plan that conflicts with the conservative defence of property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: the libertarian municipalist model leaves decisions with local assemblies, where fundamentalists want binding religious law.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Pharmaceutical regulation has no doctrinal tie.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred: scriptural views of mortality and creation make transhumanist life extension a low priority or objectionable.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Financial privacy has no doctrinal tie.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist movements favour moral regulation of online conduct, but also use anonymity against hostile states.

person-over-state.rationale: Fundamentalists hold the individual answers to God and the community, yet reject treating persons merely as means; split on the personalist claim.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal structure has no doctrinal answer.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not addressed, though some religious groups object to tampering with creation.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning has no doctrinal tie.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Faith, not race, is the dividing line in universalist fundamentalisms, though some ethnoreligious strands differ.

racial-pride.rationale: Ancestry pride is not a religious claim; some ethnoreligious strands endorse it and universal faiths often do not.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Militant strands accept expansion and holy war, while Protestant and Haredi fundamentalists accept only defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Faith, not language, defines the community for fundamentalists, who reject the language-based nation in favour of religion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate electorates serve religious communities in India and Pakistan, but are not a shared fundamentalist position.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Some movements fear foreign plots, but the sources show no shared claim.

free-public-college.rationale: Higher education finance has no doctrinal link.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from alignment with anti-tax and anti-environmental regulation positions in the largest strand.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: stewardship of creation is a theme in the scriptures, so duty to hand on the Earth undamaged is plausible but not stated.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms policy has no doctrinal link.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomatic secrecy is not a religious issue.

capital-controls.rationale: Financial regulation has no doctrinal link.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Religious militias exist in Hezbollah and others, while American fundamentalists favour armed citizens; the family splits.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists accept holy and just war and revere obedience, so urging soldiers to refuse war is not theirs.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour bargaining is not a fundamentalist issue.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credit design has no doctrinal link, though pro-family support appeals.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Islamist writers criticise Western economic dominance but Protestant fundamentalists do not; split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Revolutionary Islamists and Khomeinists replace the state, while most other fundamentalists seek to use it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Pluralism of economic systems is not a religious doctrine.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Environmental accounting has no doctrinal link.

sacred-nation.rationale: Hindu and religious-Zionist nationalism sanctify the nation, while Protestant and Salafi fundamentalists regard that as idolatrous.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No doctrine; conservatives usually oppose it while scriptural jubilee supports forgiveness.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Fundamentalists teach humans are made in God's image with a fixed nature, so redesigning nature is rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalists distrust secular media and prefer religious broadcasting, but may accept state media under religious control.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural support has no doctrinal link, though rural religious constituencies often benefit.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: religious identity, not class, is the basis of political organisation for fundamentalists.

ban-fgm.rationale: Practice is claimed by some religious traditions but others condemn it; no common fundamentalist stance exists across the family.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: fundamentalist family programs keep distinct roles, and traditional inheritance rules often unequal, but Protestant fundamentalists accept equal property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Linguistic classification has no doctrinal link.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental legal design has no doctrinal link.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Traditional religious authorities advising lawmaking resembles clerical councils, but this is not a shared position.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: prioritising environment over liberty is not part of the faith-based agenda, which holds moral order and religious liberty first.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: fixed penalties suit the moral-law outlook, though the sources do not discuss sentencing.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Right-to-work rules are not a fundamentalist issue, though US conservatives favour them.

voter-id.rationale: Election administration is not a fundamentalist question.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Fundamentalists hold their own interpretation is true; the Fundamentalism Project calls them absolutist, so equal legal standing for all readings is rejected.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Fundamentalists differ on whether elections alone suffice; Islamist parties accept electoral procedure while denying that outcomes may contradict religious law.

premarital-sex.rationale: Tarducci identifies sexual roles and family reorganisation as shared fundamentalist concerns, so sex outside marriage is rejected for women especially.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Depends on whether the movement rules; religious states cut access, opposition movements decry it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design has no doctrinal link.

women-suffrage.rationale: Early American fundamentalists mostly accepted women's vote, while some Islamist and Haredi groups restrict women's political roles; split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Tarducci describes gender roles as part of fundamentalists' religious ordering of society, and adherents regard it as honouring women, rejecting the claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: Racial categories are not addressed in sources, and fundamentalists neither affirm nor deny them as doctrine.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Dedicated state agencies promoting gender equality conflict with the fundamentalist model of distinct roles.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Wikipedia records that Christian fundamentalists refused to group Christianity with Islam and Judaism as one Abrahamic family, and The Fundamentals treated other religions and sects as errors, so one underlying truth is denied.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Literal inerrancy is the first of the five fundamentals and Article XII-style affirmations of the Chicago Statement; no current statement asks about it directly.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Fundamentalism is not defined by a property theory; traditions diverge, so inferred as neutral.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its suspicion of secular supranational authority; traditions differ.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender roles and family order are shared features of fundamentalisms, so guaranteeing equality as a secular rule runs against them.

defend-planned-state.rationale: It opposes atheistic regimes but economic views vary widely by tradition; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Preferences on constitutional design differ across traditions; inferred as neutral.

national-church-status.rationale: Fundamentalists want their scripture to shape public life, though American Protestants often oppose establishment, so adherents are split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Varies by tradition and territory; inferred as neutral.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Varies by tradition and territory; inferred as neutral.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Varies by tradition; inferred as neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Asceticism appears in some traditions but not others; adherents split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Varies by tradition; inferred as neutral.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its traditional gender order; adherents differ on drafting women.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: attachment to sacred land is strong in Jewish and Hindu variants but not a defining mark of Protestant or Islamic fundamentalism, so adherents are split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: some fundamentalist movements back harsh punishment of vice, others stress due process under divine law, so adherents are split.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: foreign alignment follows each country's circumstances, not the shared fundamentalist core, so it is unsettled.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: support for co-religionists abroad is common but the statement is about co-nationals, and traditions diverge.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: scriptural traditions hold that land belongs to God but differ on economics, so adherents are split.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the view that body and labour belong to God and are bound by divine law, not owned outright; traditions vary.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Economic preferences differ widely by tradition and this issue is not part of the fundamentalist core.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: religious charity is valued, but whether it is means-tested or universal is not a fundamentalist question.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: movements typically look to clergy and religious organisations as intermediaries rather than direct leader-to-people rule; strands differ.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not addressed by the fundamentalist core, and economic positions differ by tradition.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the aim of making religion the basis of public life, which favours religiously organised politics over cross-cutting ones.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Fundamentalism Project describes fundamentalists as selectively using modern technology and organisation while rejecting modernist values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Fundamentalists defend traditional family and gender roles under scripture or religious law, which usually leaves divorce with the husband or requires religious process.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: national resource policy is not a fundamentalist concern and economic stances differ widely by tradition.

missingStatements.text: Scripture is the inerrant word of God and is to be read literally.
missingStatements.rationale: Literal inerrancy is the first of the five fundamentals and Article XII-style affirmations of the Chicago Statement; no current statement asks about it directly.

missingStatements.text: Scientific theories and historical criticism should not be allowed to overturn what scripture teaches.
missingStatements.rationale: The Chicago Statement denies that scientific hypotheses or source criticism may overturn scripture, and The Fundamentals opposed higher criticism.

missingStatements.text: Religious believers should keep a sharp boundary between themselves and those who reject the core doctrines of their faith.
missingStatements.rationale: Wikipedia and the Fundamentalism Project describe strong in-group and out-group lines and absolutism as defining marks.
missingStatements.declined: Hard to word neutrally; other statements on religion in public life capture the contrast.

notes: Fundamentalism is a pejorative-tinged scholarly label, and traditions answer differently on state form, clerical rule, apostasy, women's dress and territory. Most economic, procedural and foreign-policy statements are left at 0 or low confidence because the family has no shared doctrine on them.
